summary.en: Manipur chief minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh seized a Kuki-Zo insurgent camp, arrested 17 suspects accused of impersonating SoO cadres, and confiscated weapons while urging surrender of illegal arms and linking gun culture to ongoing violence. The Kashmir IGP called for action against over-ground workers and hybrid terrorists, urging police to become more intelligence driven. Congress demanded the resignation of the Manipur chief minister, fresh elections and dissolution of the assembly. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Manipur statsminister Yumnam Khemchand Singh tok over en Kuki-Zo-opprørsleir, arresterte 17 mistenkte som ble anklaget for å utgi seg for SoO-kader, og konfiskerte våpen mens han oppfordret til overgivelse av ulovlige våpen og knyttet skytevåpenkulturen til den pågående volden. I Kashmir oppfordret IGP til handling mot over-grunnsarbeidere og hybride terrorister, og ba politiet bli mer etterretningsdrevet. Kongressen krevde at Manipur statsminister måtte gå av, friske valg og oppløsning av forsamlingen. UCDP registrerte 437 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
